questions.question: In a fresh R session, a student runs only the line `g <- function(x) { print("start"); x * 2 }`. What appears in the console?
options: `[1] "start"`, because R runs the body once to check it while storing `g`.
Nothing: the line creates the function object `g` and runs none of its body.
An error, because the argument `x` has no value at the moment the line runs.
The code of `g`, which R displays to confirm the definition it has stored.

questions.question: In a fresh R session, a student first runs the line `half(10)` and only afterwards the line `half <- function(x) { x / 2 }`. What does the first line give?
options: The error `could not find function "half"`, as `half` does not exist yet.
`[1] 5`, because R reads all definitions in a script before it runs any call.
The error `object 'x' not found`, because `x` is only defined by the later line.
`NULL`, because R returns an empty value for any name it has not seen before.

questions.question: A student runs `rate <- function(cost, n) { cost / n }`. Which statement about `cost` and `n` in this definition is correct?
options: They take their values from global objects called `cost` and `n` if those exist.
They become objects in the Global Environment as soon as the definition is run.
They are placeholders filled by the values of a call such as `rate(50, 10)`.
They are the outputs of `rate()`, while `cost / n` is the input it receives.

questions.question: After `sq <- function(x) { x^2 }`, what does `sq(c(1, 2, 3))` return?
options: the error `unused arguments (2, 3)`

questions.question: Which line defines a function `ratio` so that `ratio(6, 3)` returns `[1] 2`?
options: `ratio(a, b) <- { a / b }`
`ratio <- function(a, b) { a / b }`
`function ratio(a, b) { a / b }`
`ratio <- function(a, b) return a / b`

questions.question: After `g <- function(n, p) { n * p }`, which line shows only the code inside the braces of `g`, without the argument list?
options: `body(g)`
`formals(g)`

questions.question: A student ran `area <- function(r) { 3 * r^2 }`, then changed `3` to `pi` in the script and saved the file, but did not run the line again. What does `area(2)` return now?
options: the error `could not find function "area"`
the error `object 'r' not found`

questions.question: The lines `v <- c(4, 9); max(v) - min(v)` work, and `v` still exists. Which definition makes `rng(c(1, 5))` return `[1] 4`?
options: `rng <- function(v) { max(c(4, 9)) - min(c(4, 9)) }`
`rng <- function() { max(v) - min(v) }`
`rng <- function(x) { max(v) - min(v) }`
`rng <- function(v) { max(v) - min(v) }`

questions.question: After `f <- function(v) { out <- 0; for (i in v) { out <- out + i^2 }; return(out) }`, what does `f(c(1, 2, 3))` return?
After `own_sum <- function(xvec) { out <- 0; for (i in xvec) { out <- out + i }; out }` and `wage <- c(3, 5)`, a student types `own_sum(wages)`. What happens?
options: the error `object 'wages' not found`
the error `could not find function "own_sum"`
the error `argument "xvec" is missing, with no default`

questions.question: A student runs the line `function(x) { x^2 }` on its own, without `sq <-` in front. What does this line do?
options: R stops with an error, since a definition must start with a name and `<-`.
R stores the function in the Global Environment, where it appears without a name.
R prints nothing, since running a function definition never shows any output.
R prints the new function but stores it nowhere, so no later line can call it.

questions.question: For `own_avg <- function(xvec) { sum(xvec) / length(xvec) }`, `formals(own_avg)` lists the argument `xvec` with nothing after its name. What does the empty value mean?
options: `xvec` currently holds an empty vector, so the call `own_avg()` returns `NaN`.
`xvec` is optional: if it is left out, R fills it with the vector in use last time.
`xvec` has no default value, so every call of `own_avg()` must supply it.
`xvec` is not used yet, because the function has not been called so far.

questions.question: What does R print at the end of `f <- function(x) { x + 1 }; a <- f(2); f <- function(x) { x * 10 }; c(a, f(2))`?
options: an error, because the name `f` already holds a function

questions.question: To check it against `sum()`, a student defines `own_total <- function(x) { out <- 0; for (i in 1:length(x)) { out <- out + i }; out }`. What does `own_total(c(10, 20, 30))` return?
After `own_sum <- function(xvec) { out <- 0; for (i in xvec) { out <- out + i }; out }`, what does `own_sum(numeric(0))` return for the empty numeric vector?
options: `numeric(0)`
`NULL`

questions.question: After `own_sum <- function(xvec) { out <- 0; for (i in xvec) { out <- out + i }; out }`, what does `own_sum(matrix(1:4, nrow = 2))` return?
options: an error, because `xvec` was meant to be a vector

questions.question: `own_colsum()` calls `own_sum()` in its body. A student corrects a bug in `own_sum()` and reruns only that definition, not the one of `own_colsum()`. Which statement about the next call `own_colsum(X)` is correct?
options: It uses the corrected `own_sum()`, as R looks up `own_sum` when `own_colsum()` runs.
It still uses the old `own_sum()`, copied into `own_colsum()` when that was defined.
It fails with `could not find function "own_sum"`, as the old version was replaced.
It uses the corrected version only if `own_sum` is passed to `own_colsum()` as an argument.

questions.question: What does R print at the end of `sum <- function(v) { max(v) }; s1 <- sum(c(2, 5, 3)); rm(sum); c(s1, sum(c(2, 5, 3)))`?
options: the error `could not find function "sum"`

questions.question: `own_sum()` returns the sum of a vector. A student defines `own_rowsum <- function(m) { out <- numeric(nrow(m)); for (i in 1:nrow(m)) { out[i] <- own_sum(m[i, ]) }; out }`. What does `own_rowsum(matrix(1:6, nrow = 2))` return?
After `gap <- function(x, y) { x - y }; x <- 2; y <- 9`, what does `gap(y, x)` return?
options: the error `formal argument "x" matched by multiple actual arguments`
`[1] 7`, with a warning that `y` was passed to the argument `x`
